page.title: Figma: The collaborative canvas for design, code, and AI

findings.title: Raster buried under a wash or opacity (×4)
findings.evidence: “ at opacity 0 "Wireframe of a website"” · “ at opacity 0 "Butterfly illustration"” · “ at opacity 0 "Personal portfolio website pulled up on an ipad"”
findings.fix: A background image under a near-opaque gradient wash, or a raster on an element at near-zero opacity, never reaches the screen: the page shows the wash, and the produced texture or photo ships as a compliance token. Let the material show (a tint under 0.9 alpha, a blend mode, an opacity you can see) or remove the file.

findings.title: 5 tracked all-caps section labels
findings.evidence: Small uppercase, letter-spaced labels like “New” above sections. On 10.5% of Show HN launches, and usually redundant with the heading under them.
findings.fix: Delete the label or fold its word into the heading.

findings.title: h2 is used at 2 sizes, consistently
findings.evidence: Sizes: 30px ×4, 44px ×13. “The products you love are designed in Figma” is 44px, “Move fast in the right direction on an AI-native c” is 30px. Each size is used more than once, so this is a system rather than drift; but it means the same tag is doing two jobs.
findings.fix: If the 30px ones are sub-sections, make them h3. Screen readers and search engines only see the tag.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: Above-the-fold is visually busy
findings.evidence: Quadtree decomposition of the first screen (text and photos masked out) needs 757 leaves (calm pages run 50–250; busy ones 600+). Whitespace share 81%, text covers 15% of the viewport.
findings.fix: Remove one thing from the first screen. Reinecke's data says people rate low- and medium-complexity pages the same and punish high complexity; the gain is all in cutting, not adding.
findings.citation: Reinecke et al. CHI 2013; Tuch et al.: complexity drives the 50ms impression

findings.title: Repeating-gradient stripes
findings.fix: Repeating-gradient stripes used as surface decoration are a recurring generated-UI signature. Reach for a deliberate texture or leave the surface plain.
